about: The original Ashton blend, made for Ashton by the Fuente family in the Dominican Republic. It pairs a golden Connecticut Shade wrapper with Dominican binder and filler aged three to four years and is the brand's mildest core line.
notes: Ashton's own site simply calls this line Ashton; Classic is the common shop name. The maker lists 13 sizes, also including Monarch (6 x 50), Crystal No. 1 (6.5 x 44) and Sovereign (6.75 x 55).
verifyNotes: Fields confirmed. Ashton's and Holt's pages do not say where the wrapper is grown, so swapped the Holt's link for Neptune, which lists USA Connecticut Shade.

about: A longer-aged step up from the core Ashton blend, made by the Fuente family. Dominican tobaccos aged five to seven years sit under a Connecticut Shade wrapper, and several sizes are perfectos and figurados.
notes: The maker also lists a No. 1 at 9 x 52.
verifyNotes: Fields confirmed. Added Neptune as the source for the USA-grown wrapper, which Ashton's and Holt's pages do not state.

about: Ashton's maduro line, made by the Fuente family with a slow-fermented Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper over aged Dominican tobaccos. It is a sweet, mellow maduro rather than a strong one.

about: Ashton's top-priced line, an all-Dominican cigar made by the Fuente family with a wrapper from their Chateau de la Fuente farm. It was created for Ashton's 20th anniversary, and each size is named as a yearly salute.
notes: ESG stands for Estate Sun Grown. The wrapper comes from the same Fuente farm that grows Fuente Fuente OpusX wrapper. Made in small batches, so supply can be tight.

about: Ashton's full-bodied line, made by the Fuente family since 1999. A dark Sumatra-seed wrapper grown on a private estate in Ecuador covers Dominican binder and filler aged four to five years.
notes: VSG stands for Virgin Sun Grown. Most sizes are box-pressed. The maker also lists Enchantment (4.375 x 60) and Illusion (6.5 x 44).

about: A medium-bodied Ashton made by the Fuente family with a reddish Cuban-seed wrapper grown in Ecuador over Dominican binder and filler. Puro Sol refers to the tobaccos all being grown in full sun.
Released in 2014 as the first new Ashton line in close to a decade, blended by Carlito Fuente. It was the first Ashton to use Nicaraguan tobacco, set under an Ecuador Habano Rosado wrapper.
notes: Ashton's site and Holt's now list strength as Full. At launch Ashton described it as medium to full.

notes: Strength varies by source: Neptune's spec says medium, Holt's medium-full, and a halfwheel reviewer found the 7 x 70 mild to medium. Halfwheel and Neptune place production in Nicaragua, while Holt's says Honduras. Asylum writes sizes ring gauge first.

about: AVO's series of annual limited editions, usually released in March around Avo Uvezian's birthday. It followed the older AVO LE releases, and every year was a different blend and size made by Davidoff in the Dominican Republic.
notes: This is a series, not one blend, so there is no single wrapper or strength. It began in 2015 with the Classic Covers releases, used the Improvisation name from LE17 through LE21, and closed in 2022 with the LE22 White and Black. Ask which year a given box is.

about: Introduced at the 2010 IPCPR show and billed as the strongest AVO to that point, at a lower price than the rest of the range. A sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper covers Dominican and Peruvian tobaccos, made by Davidoff.

about: A richer AVO made by Davidoff that used tobacco from Avo Uvezian's own Dominican farm, Domaine AVO, under a sun grown Ecuadorian wrapper. Its shapes included perfectos.
